alternatives.label: European Integration, History and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: Political and historical foundations lead into European integration and law. Statistics and introductory economics prepare for macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics and econometrics. Literature and media add ways to examine representation.
alternatives.concept: Study how European institutions, markets and political identities developed. Combine EU politics and law with European and global history, comparative politics, economics and the study of cultural representation.
progression: Political and historical foundations lead into European integration and law. Statistics and introductory economics prepare for macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics and econometrics. Literature and media add ways to examine representation.

alternatives.label: European Culture, History and Representation
alternatives.labelReason: Introductory history, literature and media analysis support work on empire, travel writing and changing media forms. Qualitative methods support advanced cultural analysis, documentary and historical research. EU politics supplies institutional context.
alternatives.concept: Study how ideas about Europe are made and contested in literature, film, history and public life. Compare narratives of empire, gender, race and belonging, and use historical and qualitative research to examine how those narratives shape societies.
progression: Introductory history, literature and media analysis support work on empire, travel writing and changing media forms. Qualitative methods support advanced cultural analysis, documentary and historical research. EU politics supplies institutional context.
alternatives.distinctness: Literary, film and cultural analysis and historical research receive substantially more weight than economic modelling or legal doctrine.

alternatives.label: European Law, Institutions and Democratic Justice
alternatives.concept: Study how European institutions govern and how their decisions affect rights and participation. Connect EU and international law, comparative constitutional law and legal reasoning with European politics, civic movements and public ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The law gateway precedes constitutional, international, private, criminal and EU law. Entrepreneurship prepares for transnational business law. History, sociology and ethics support analysis of justice, democratic institutions and social movements.
progression: The law gateway precedes constitutional, international, private, criminal and EU law. Entrepreneurship prepares for transnational business law. History, sociology and ethics support analysis of justice, democratic institutions and social movements.
alternatives.distinctness: Legal doctrine, comparative legal analysis and rights receive substantially more weight than political economy or cultural analysis.

blocks: EU law gives a legal perspective on integration. UvA specifically studies integration and enlargement theories.
Both examine European Union institutions and democratic governance. UvA also studies integration in historical perspective.
The 12 EC slot is filled through an eligible second-major choice.
Both use historical context to explain political and social change. UvA focuses explicitly on the construction of Europe.

UCR’s social theory course provides tools for studying civil society and collective identities. UvA centres European identities and cultures.
Both use travel writing and related narratives to examine identity and cultural boundaries. UvA explicitly studies ideas of Europe.
Both analyse how literature and film represent a subject. UvA centres literary and cinematic representations of a European city.

selection.assessment: The broad option covers European institutions, history, identity and political economy. The other two options give greater weight to culture and historical inquiry, or legal institutions and democratic justice. Eastern Europe has insufficient sustained regional depth. The three options do not reproduce UvA’s required language sequence.

notes.text: UvA requires a four-course sequence in one modern language. The UCR options do not include a corresponding language sequence.

UvA combines European Studies core courses with European Culture, a second-major choice and a thesis. The UCR options build related pathways from courses in several fields. Independent research at UCR is optional.

audience.programmeDescription: European Studies at the University of Amsterdam examines how Europe’s institutions, histories and cultures have developed. This example follows the European Culture major and includes language study, coursework from a second major and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines European politics and law with history, economics and cultural analysis. The other options focus on representation and historical inquiry, or on law and democratic institutions. Several UCR courses draw on examples outside Europe.
